pregnancy_lactation.statement: 'As there is no information on reproductive and developmental toxicity, the use during pregnancy and lactation cannot be recommended' (EMA). EMA's thujone statement adds that use of thujone-containing products in pregnant women and children should be minimised.
pregnancy_lactation.md: 'As there is no information on reproductive and developmental toxicity, the use during pregnancy and lactation cannot be recommended' (EMA). EMA's [thujone](#term:thujone) statement adds that use of thujone-containing products in pregnant women and children should be minimised.

adverse_event_history.statement: A toddler developed tonic-clonic seizures after home-made sage tea; EMA also records epileptiform convulsions after prolonged use of alcoholic extracts or pure oil, and convulsions in rats at high sage-oil doses.
adverse_event_history.md: A toddler developed tonic-clonic [seizures](#term:convulsant) after home-made sage tea; EMA also records epileptiform convulsions after prolonged use of alcoholic extracts or pure oil, and convulsions in rats at high sage-oil doses.

constituents_of_concern.threshold_or_limit: 3.5 mg/day or 6.6 mg/day thujone (EMA derivations); 3-7 mg/day stated to pose no special concern

constituents_of_concern.concern: convulsant at high exposure; 7-50 % of commercial sage oils
constituents_of_concern.threshold_or_limit: EMA toxicity thresholds ~5 mg/kg (insignificant) and >30 mg/kg (manifest toxicity), reported in the rosemary report
constituents_of_concern.md: convulsant at high exposure; 7-50 % of commercial sage oils

evidence.claim: A sage extract reduced menopausal hot-flush severity and overall menopausal complaints compared with placebo.
evidence.test_article_detail: Menosan (ethanolic S. officinalis extract tablets), 4 weeks
evidence.outcome_summary: Menopause Rating Scale -39.2 % vs -6.3 %; hot-flush severity -55.3 % (80 randomised, 48 per protocol).

md.claim: A sage extract reduced menopausal hot-flush severity and overall menopausal complaints compared with [placebo](#term:placebo).
md.outcome_summary: Menopause Rating Scale -39.2 % vs -6.3 %; hot-flush severity -55.3 % (80 [randomised](#term:rct), 48 per protocol).

evidence.claim: Hot-flush intensity fell during 8 weeks of a fresh sage leaf tablet in an uncontrolled study.
evidence.test_article_detail: once-daily fresh sage leaf tablet, open multicentre, no control
evidence.outcome_summary: Hot-flush intensity score -50 % at 4 weeks, -64 % at 8 weeks (ITT n = 69).
evidence.note: No placebo arm; EMA did not accept it for well-established use [1].

md.claim: Hot-flush intensity fell during 8 weeks of a fresh sage leaf tablet in an [uncontrolled](#term:open-label) study.
md.outcome_summary: Hot-flush intensity score -50 % at 4 weeks, -64 % at 8 weeks (ITT n = 69).

evidence.claim: Sage extract improved cognition in mild to moderate Alzheimer's disease over 4 months.
evidence.outcome_summary: Better ADAS-cog and CDR-SB than placebo (n = 42); more agitation on sage.
evidence.note: Single small trial; a systematic review found benefits undermined by methodological issues and heterogeneous preparations [53].

md.claim: Sage extract improved cognition in mild to moderate Alzheimer's disease over 4 months.
md.outcome_summary: Better ADAS-cog and CDR-SB than placebo (n = 42); more agitation on sage.

evidence.claim: Dried sage leaf changed mood and alertness acutely in healthy adults.
evidence.test_article_detail: dried S. officinalis leaf in capsules, two amounts, crossover
evidence.outcome_summary: Improved mood; anxiety/alertness effects differed by amount (n = 30).
evidence.note: Test article matters: other cognition trials used extracts, oils or S. lavandulaefolia [53].

md.claim: Dried sage leaf changed mood and alertness acutely in healthy adults.
md.outcome_summary: Improved mood; anxiety/alertness effects differed by amount (n = 30).

evidence.claim: A sage spray eased acute pharyngitis pain slightly more than placebo.
evidence.test_article_detail: 15 % sage spray (Hubbert et al. 2006, as described by EMA)
evidence.outcome_summary: About 44 % vs 34 % pain reduction within 2 hours.
evidence.note: Primary paper not read; EMA notes the concentration differs from EU-marketed products.

md.claim: A sage spray eased acute pharyngitis pain slightly more than placebo.
md.outcome_summary: About 44 % vs 34 % pain reduction within 2 hours.

evidence.claim: Sage leaf is traditionally used for mild dyspepsia, excessive sweating, mouth/throat inflammation and minor skin inflammation.
evidence.outcome_summary: EMA: 'relief of mild dyspeptic complaints such as heartburn and bloating'; 'relief of excessive sweating'; 'relief of inflammations in the mouth or the throat'.

md.claim: Sage leaf is [traditionally used](#term:traditional-use) for mild dyspepsia, excessive sweating, mouth/throat inflammation and minor skin inflammation.
md.outcome_summary: EMA: 'relief of mild dyspeptic complaints such as heartburn and bloating'; 'relief of excessive sweating'; 'relief of inflammations in the mouth or the throat'.
